text.p: German construction company Philipp Holzmann AG plans to swing back into profit with a sustained programme of cost reduction, the company said in an interview with Germany's Boersen Zeitung on Saturday.
Holzmann's management board chairman Lothar Mayer and its new chief financial officer Rainer Klee said the group planned to dispose of property holdings worth two billion marks.
To this end, the group said it had found a buyer for its portfolio of 4,000 apartments.
Mayer said in the report the cost-cutting programme would continue until the end of 1997 and the group hoped to be reporting an operating profit from the beginning of 1998.
A spokesman for the company told Reuters the proceeds from the sale of the property holdings would for the most part counteract the effect on earnings from the group's restructuring programme.
The spokesman would not comment on the price of the apartments.
Holzmann made losses of 443 million marks in 1995 following huge write-downs for losses on real estate projects.
